# Honey bee colonies exercise {#honeybeechap}
![](/images/bee_1.png){style="width:200px; background: white; border-radius:5px; border: white solid 5px"}
Next we have a file ([honey_bee.tsv](https://neof-workshops.github.io/R_j4c0xh/downloads/honey_bee.tsv)) that contains information on the number of Honey Bee colonies in 4 different USA states. It is temporal data containing information on the 4 quarters for the years 2015-2018. For more details and even more data please see the following link: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/kyleahmurphy/nass-honey-bee-20152021 Solutions are in the expandable boxes. Try your best to solve each challenge but use the solutions for help if you would like. Even if your method works it can be good to check the solution as there are many ways to do the same thing in R ## Honey bee colony challenges ### Honey bee colony challenge 1 {-}
![](/images/bee_2.png){style="width:150px; background: white; border-radius:5px; border: white solid 5px"}
__Read__ in the file "honey_bee.tsv" as a __data frame__ __variable__ called "bee_colonies_df". Ensure the row names contain the Year info (2015-Q1, 2015-Q2, etc.).
Read in file: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} bee_colonies_df <- read.csv("Chapter_8_files/honey_bee.tsv", sep = "\t", row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE) ``` :::
### Honey bee colony challenge 2 {-}
![](/images/bee_3.png){style="width:150px; background: white; border-radius:5px; border: white solid 5px"}
Create a __data frame__ called "bee_colonies_2017_2018_df" containing the rows for 2017 & 2018 from "bee_colonies_df".
Create 2017 & 2018 __data frame__: Read in file: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} #Can index to get the desired columns bee_colonies_2017_2018_df <- bee_colonies_df[9:16,] #Alternatively the tail() function can be used #It is like head() but will get lowest rows bee_colonies_2017_2018_df <- tail(bee_colonies_df, n = 8) ``` :::
### Honey bee colony challenge 3 {-}
![](/images/bee_4.png){style="width:200px; background: white; border-radius:5px; border: white solid 5px"}
For each month in 2017 & 2018 print out the phrase "The number of colonies in Minnesota for \ was \. - For example, the first phrase will be "The number of colonies in Minnesota for 2017-Q1 was 27000". - This can be done with one line of code using the `paste()` function.
::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} paste("The number of colonies in Minnesota for", row.names(bee_colonies_2017_2018_df), "was", bee_colonies_2017_2018_df$Minnesota, sep = " ") ``` :::
### Honey bee colony challenge 4 {-}
![](/images/bee_5.png){style="width:150px; background: white; border-radius:5px; border: white solid 5px"}
Make an average (mean) row for "bee_colonies_2017_2018_df".
Mean row: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} bee_colonies_2017_2018_df["Average",] <- colMeans(bee_colonies_2017_2018_df) ``` :::
### Honey bee colony challenge 5 {-}
![](/images/bee_6.png){style="width:200px; background: white; border-radius:5px; border: white solid 5px"}
Finally write out the __data frame__ "bee_colonies_2017_2018_df" as a tab separated file called "bee_colonies_2017_2018.tsv".
Write out file: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} write.table(bee_colonies_2017_2018_df, "Chapter_8_files/bee_colonies_2017_2018.tsv", sep = "\t", col.names = NA, quote = FALSE) ``` :::
## Honey bee colony MCQs
![](/images/question_bubble_orange.png){style="width:200px; background: white; border-radius:5px; border: white solid 5px"}
Great! Using files and subsetting are very important skills in R so I hope the challenges helped improve your skills and confidence. Now that you have carried out the challenges, attempt the following questions based on the "bee_colonies_2017_2018_df" object. ::: {.cell} ::: 1. Which state has the lowest average?
::: {.cell} ::: 2. Which state has the highest minimum value of colonies?
::: {.cell} ::: 3. Which state had 20,000 colonies in Q3 of 2018 (2018-Q3)?
__Tip__: If you use the `summary()` function, ensure you do not include the "Average" row.
You can figure out the MCQs by viewing the data frame. However, you can also figure them out with R code. Below are commands to get the answers for the MCQs. I will let you decipher them yourself. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} #Question 1: Which state has the lowest average? min_average <- min(bee_colonies_2017_2018_df["Average",]) states <- colnames(bee_colonies_2017_2018_df) min_average_state <- states[ bee_colonies_2017_2018_df["Average",] == min_average] min_average_state ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} #Question 2: Which state has the highest minimum value of colonies? bee_summary <- summary(bee_colonies_2017_2018_df[1:8,]) bee_summary ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} #Question 3: Which state had 20,000 colonies in Q3 of 2018 (2018-Q3)? n <- 20000 column_logical_vec <- bee_colonies_2017_2018_df["2018-Q3",] == n column_logical_vec colnames(bee_colonies_2017_2018_df)[column_logical_vec] ``` :::
